question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(85,0.56),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X=50).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6628\,$ | $\,0.6664\,$ | $\,0.6700\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.6985\,$ | $\,0.7019\,$ | $\,0.7054\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ | $\,0.7357\,$ | $\,0.7389\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=85$ and $p=0.56.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =85\cdot 0.56 \\  & =47.6 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =85\cdot (1-0.56) \\  & =37.4 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(85)(0.56)=47.6
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(85)(0.56)(1-0.56)=20.94.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(47.6,20.94).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=50).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=50)≈P(49.5\le Y\le 50.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(49.5\le Y\le 50.5) & =P(\frac{49.5-47.6}{\sqrt{20.94}}\le Z\le \frac{50.5-47.6}{\sqrt{20.94}}) \\  & ≈P(0.42\le Z\le 0.63) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.63)-P(Z<0.42) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.63)-P(Z\le 0.42) \\  & =Φ(0.63)-Φ(0.42) \\  & =0.7357-0.6628 \\  & =0.073\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=50)≈0.073.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0758.$
